findings.issue: Step 1 states the greater-reduction-potential cathode rule without limiting it to a galvanic cell, and the Full-credit answer echoes that unqualified context. This rule selects the favored galvanic pairing; an electrolytic cell can use an applied potential to force the unfavored pairing. Add “in a galvanic cell” to the rule and keep part (1) of the worked answer in that context.
findings.evidence: SOURCE 9.9 answer_move explicitly says to choose the reduction with the greater reduction potential “for the cathode in a galvanic cell.” CED 9.8 and 9.9 distinguish favored galvanic reactions from unfavored electrolytic reactions requiring an externally applied potential.
